records.name: Pennsylvania Registry of Interpreters for the Deaf
records.summary: A volunteer-run Pennsylvania group that supports sign language interpreters and works to improve communication access for Deaf, hard of hearing, and DeafBlind people. It holds regional summits, board meetings, and an annual membership meeting, many of them on Zoom.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for one of four committees (communications, Deaf interpreters, emerging interpreters, or professional development) through the group's online form, attend a board meeting or the annual membership meeting on Zoom, or apply for membership online or on paper.

schedule.text: Board meetings and the annual membership meeting are held on Zoom.

cost.text: The site does not list membership dues. Graduates of the Pennsylvania Interpreter Training Program, and Pennsylvania interpreters who recently earned their first national interpreter certification, may get a free one-year membership. Other event fees are set for each event.

first_step.how: Sign up for a committee through the group's online form, or email membership@parid.org to ask about joining.
first_step.basis: Committee sign-up and membership questions have clear public contacts, and non-members can register for the summit, but membership needs an application and the site does not say whether non-members may attend board meetings.
first_step.what_to_expect: Its board and membership meetings are held on Zoom, and the November board meeting is conducted in ASL only, so you will need to register through the event page. The regional summit in Pittsburgh on October 9 and 10, 2026 is a two-day paid conference with workshops, and non-members can register at a higher rate than members.
first_visit_tips: Register through the event page, since the Zoom link comes in the confirmation email.
If you need access support, email recorder@parid.org before the accommodation deadline printed on the event page.
Ask about the free one-year membership if you recently earned a first national interpreter certification or graduated from a Pennsylvania interpreter training program.

access.notes: Board meetings are conducted in ASL only. Accommodation requests for meetings go to recorder@parid.org by the deadline printed on each event page.

records.notes: The regional summit is in Pittsburgh, not Philadelphia. The tier 1 note that several committees were on hiatus is outdated: the homepage still says some are on hiatus, but the committees page lists four committees with sign-up forms and says the information sessions were canceled. Two IRS mailing addresses are on file and both are kept. Non-member access to board meetings is not stated. The contact name Sarah Reed was carried from tier 1 and is not named on the pages read.

records.name: Mid-Atlantic Eurasia Business Council
records.summary: A business council that links Mid-Atlantic companies with partners in Eurasia, mostly through trade events, seminars and delegations. It also holds public cultural and remembrance events, including programs about people who rescued Jews during the Holocaust.
records.what_you_do: Attend a Carl Lutz event (the site invites the public to some of them), register for a seminar or trade event, or apply for a company membership by mail. The site also lists internships.

schedule.text: Seminars, roundtables, trade events and commemorations are posted on the site as each one is planned, so dates vary from year to year.

cost.text: Company membership dues run from $250 to $950 a year depending on company revenue, with a $2,000 sponsorship level and a $100 yearly rate for nonprofits. Members get 20 percent off the council's events. Some public events are free and others need a paid registration.

first_step.how: Register for a public Carl Lutz event on the site, or call 484-467-7444 or email info@ma-rbc.org to ask about attending a seminar.
first_step.basis: Public events have registration links and the council lists a phone and email, but membership is an application aimed at companies.
first_step.what_to_expect: Public events are mostly talks, seminars and commemorations rather than hands-on activities. The October 2026 Carl Lutz program lists remarks by a speaker and a film screening, and many listings leave out the time or fee. Read the linked flyer before you go.
first_visit_tips: Register from the event listing when one is given, since some events use a Zoom sign-up link.
Look in the linked flyers for the start time and fee, because the event pages often leave them out.
Ask the council before you apply for membership, since the form is for companies and is mailed with a check.

records.notes: Membership is for companies (dues by revenue, $100 a year for nonprofits). The benefits page names a Nonprofit/Individual Membership option that the application page does not list, so ask the council whether individuals can join. Many event times, venues and fees sit in linked PDFs that were not read. The Carl Lutz exhibit end date conflicts on the site (a summer 2026 close in one notice, fall 2026 in another). The events page is mostly an archive of 2005 to 2009 events and was not used as current evidence. The homepage was cut off after 100,000 characters, so its oldest items were not read.

records.name: Pennsylvania Education for All Coalition
records.summary: A nonprofit, founded in 2000, that helps families get the school support children with disabilities need. It offers free help with IEPs, runs networks for parents and self advocates, and works for children to learn in their neighborhood schools.
records.what_you_do: Register for a free IEP clinic session online, use the free education modules, or ask about becoming a Parent Consultant, a trained parent who gives free peer support to families.

schedule.text: The group holds free IEP clinics and an annual inclusion conference. Dates are posted on its events calendar as they are set.

cost.text: IEP clinic support, Parent Consultant help, and the education modules are free, and parent consultants may ask to be repaid for mileage and tolls. Donations and sponsorships are optional. The annual inclusion conference charges a fee, which was $10 to $30 for most attendees in 2026.

first_step.how: Register for a free IEP clinic session through the online form, or email info@paedforall.org to ask about joining the Parent Consultant Network.
first_step.basis: The site explains its free IEP support, how to register for a clinic, and how a parent can ask about joining its network.
first_step.what_to_expect: An IEP clinic session is a 60-minute video call with two IEP consultants. Before it, families send the student's IEP to the group, and the consultants talk through concerns, review the plan, and finish with advice and suggested next steps. The clinic is free and open to families across Pennsylvania.
first_visit_tips: Join the video call 15 minutes before your session time.
Send the IEP ahead of time and confirm the deadline, since one flyer shows an older date.
Write your top questions down, because the session is only an hour long.
Ask the group about interpreters or captioning before the session, since the clinic page does not say.

access.notes: The clinic page asks families who need accommodations to contact the group by phone or email. The clinic is listed in English and Spanish, with a Spanish-language registration form.

records.notes: The Annual Inclusion Conference (November 7, 2026 per the page, at West Chester University) is in West Chester, not Philadelphia. The Self Advocate Network is not accepting applications and has no trainings scheduled. The Spanish IEP flyer gives an October 8, 2025 deadline, which looks stale, so confirm with the group. The clinic page does not say whether live sessions run in Spanish, so no language code was recorded. The contact name Linda Carmona-Bell was carried from tier 1 and is not named on the pages read.

records.name: Philly Black Pride
records.summary: A group that puts on Pride celebrations for LGBTQ people of color in Philadelphia. Its main festival is held during the Penn Relays Carnival at the University of Pennsylvania, and it also runs year-round programs and a fund that takes donations.
records.what_you_do: Attend the PRIDE 2026 celebration (workshops, seminars, awards and nightlife events), book through the official host hotel link, or sign up for monthly updates.

schedule.text: The signature festival is held during the Penn Relays Carnival at the University of Pennsylvania each year. Other events are announced on the site as they are planned.

cost.text: Event admission and registration fees are not stated on the pages we read. The group asks for donations through its PayPal donate button and its Michael Hinson Mission Fund page.

first_step.how: Sign up for the monthly updates on the site, or email info@phillyblackpride.org to ask how to attend PRIDE 2026 or how to volunteer.
first_step.basis: Events and updates are public and there is a clear contact, but the pages do not describe how to attend events or how to volunteer.
first_step.what_to_expect: The celebration has an events program of workshops, seminars and awards, and a nightlife program of parties. The pages we read did not list 2026 dates, venues or ticket prices, so ask the group before you plan. The official host hotel is booked through a link on the PRIDE page.
first_visit_tips: Ask the group for the PRIDE 2026 dates and ticket prices before you book travel.
If you plan to stay over, use the official host hotel link on the PRIDE page.

access.notes: The accessibility statement covers the group's website only and does not describe event access, interpreting or accommodation requests.

records.notes: The contact page gives P.O. Box 22515 (19110), which differs from the IRS record (PO Box 40926, 19107). Both are kept. The Pride 365 section lists no events at the moment. The About page says COLOURS Organization, a Philadelphia health provider, started the festival in 1999, and that the group became its own nonprofit in 2004. The site shows 2026 celebration references but no month, and the footer year 2025 is not evidence, so the status stays probably_active and no last_sign_of_life is set.

records.name: Philadelphia Wind Symphony
records.summary: A volunteer wind band of about 50 players that gives around six concerts a season. Players join by audition, or sign up as substitutes.
records.what_you_do: Play in the season concerts, which run from fall into early summer. Substitutes can apply on any wind, brass or percussion part, whether or not that part is open, and they are called in as needed.

schedule.text: About six concerts a season, from fall into early summer, usually in October, December, March, May and June. Substitutes rehearse three or four times in the two weeks before each concert, with no fixed weekday.

cost.text: Audition, membership and substitute fees are not stated on the site, and concert ticket prices are not posted. Some concerts are free. The site accepts donations.

first_step.how: Apply as a substitute through the auditions page, which asks for a one-page resume and videos of your playing, or email Music Director Joe Higgins at higgins@philadelphiawindsymphony.org with questions.
first_step.basis: Seats are filled by audition and the 2026 to 2027 auditions are closed, so the way in is clear but needs a resume and playing videos before you learn what it is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Members are volunteers who play about six concerts a season at venues around the Philadelphia area. Substitutes are called as needed and rehearse three or four times in the two weeks before a concert. The site does not say how many rehearsals a substitute must attend or whether substitutes are paid.
first_visit_tips: Check the auditions page in June or July, when the group usually posts the next audition dates.
Have your resume and playing videos ready, since the substitute application asks for both.
Ask the music director how many rehearsals a substitute is expected to attend before you accept a concert.

records.notes: The concert pages print the month and day without a year. The 2026 to 2027 season heading gives the year, so the October concert is treated as October 2026. Rehearsal days and location are not published. The homepage summary mentions open flute, double bass, piano and harp positions, but the auditions page lists no open instruments, so check before applying. The IRS name is Philadelphia Chamber Winds (kept as an aka). The contact name Virginia Allen was carried from tier 1.

records.name: Philadelphia Freedom Band
records.summary: An LGBTQ+ community band with concert, marching and jazz ensembles. It welcomes players of all skill levels who share its mission.
records.what_you_do: Play in the concert band, the marching band or the jazz ensemble. The marching band plays parades around the Philadelphia region, cheers at local races in the fall and caroles at the holidays.

schedule.text: The concert band gives two free public concerts a year, one in spring and one in winter. The marching band performs in parades, cheers at races in the fall, and caroles around the holidays.

cost.text: Dues and fees are not stated on the pages we could read. The band's concerts are free to the public and include a raffle of donated items that raises money for the band.

first_step.how: Use the contact page on the band's website to ask how to join and when the next rehearsal is.
first_step.basis: The directory says the band welcomes players of every skill level and lists a contact route, but it does not publish auditions, rehearsal times or dues on the pages we could read.
first_step.what_to_expect: The concert band's two concerts a year are free and public, so you can hear the group before you join. The marching band appears in parades and at local races, so that side of the band is seen in public. Rehearsal times, dues and any audition are not published on the pages we could read, so ask the band before you come.
first_visit_tips: Ask which ensemble suits your instrument and skill level before you come to a rehearsal.
Ask for the current rehearsal schedule, since none is published on the pages we could read.

records.notes: The band's own website could not be read: both the bare and www hostnames fail the TLS certificate check, so joining steps, rehearsal times and dues are unverified and the contact page was not reached. Dated evidence is limited to the 2026 Pride Bands listing, which shows a May 2026 marching rehearsal and performance and a May 2026 festival appearance. A Free Library calendar page returned HTTP 403 and a news item did not resolve, so their details are not used. A search returned more about the band, but none of it was read, so no facts came from it. Rehearsal days and times were not found on any page read.

records.name: Philadelphia Heritage Chorale
records.summary: An intergenerational choir that sings many kinds of music, with a focus on music from the African Diaspora.
records.what_you_do: Sing with the chorale in its concerts. The site does not explain how to audition or how rehearsals work, and its events page lists no upcoming concerts.

cost.text: No singer dues or fees appear on the site. The chorale asks for donations and lists AmazonSmile and Facebook birthday fundraisers as ways to give.

first_step.how: Email PHLHeritageChorale@gmail.com and ask whether the chorale is taking new singers and how to audition.
first_step.basis: The way in is unclear: the site has no rehearsal, audition or membership details, and its newest dated item is from 2019.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe rehearsals, auditions, or how often singers meet. The group says on its events page that it plans to perform again soon, so a first visit may depend on whether it is taking new singers now. Ask by email before you plan around it.
first_visit_tips: Ask by email whether the chorale is taking new singers before you plan around it.
When you write, ask about rehearsal days, the location, and any audition or fee.

records.notes: Status moved from probably_active (tier 1) to dormant: the newest dated item the site shows is a March 2019 performance on the About page, and the copyright years are not evidence. The events page says the group plans to perform again soon, so it may be paused rather than closed. The verdict was left at publish; the owner may want to hide it if the group does not reply. The About page says the chorale has performed each year at the Kimmel Center's A Soulful Christmas, but it gives no dates. The Member Login page and the Facebook page were not used.

notes: Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used, on the Freedom Band because its own site could not be read. 40 WebFetch calls in total, at most 6 per group. No rate limiting was seen; the certificate and 403 errors affected only the Freedom Band's own domain and one library page. Verdicts: 7 publish, 0 hide. Status changes: Pennsylvania Education for All Coalition, PARID and Wind Symphony confirmed active on 2026 dated pages; Heritage Chorale moved to dormant (low confidence, flagged for owner review). The Freedom Band and Heritage Chorale records are the thinnest, because their own sites give the fewest joining details.
